behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Directed next-item transition branching of each item — the normalised entropy of its empirical successor distribution (a user-interest branching signal).

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the Stage-2 TRAINING sequences only. For every consecutive pair (u_t=i, u_{t+1}=j) inside a training session, increment n_ij. Then p_i(j)=n_ij/Σ_j' n_ij', n_i = number of distinct j with n_ij>0, and H_i = −Σ_j p_i(j) ln p_i(j) / ln(n_i) for n_i≥2; items with n_i<2 or no outgoing training pair get H_i = H̄, the mean of H over items with n_i≥2. The table is built once, frozen before Stage-2 epoch 1, and stored as a 24556-entry vector.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: H_i uses only within-session transitions of the Stage-2 training split. No validation or test interaction, no Stage-3 input, and no cross-split co-occurrence enters H_i or c_i. The curvature table and c_max are frozen before any validation/test scoring; items that appear only in validation/test receive H̄ and never contribute successor counts.

behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Behaviour-conditioned context generality: the effective number of distinct predecessor contexts of an item, exp(H_i), from directed item-to-item transitions in the training split; because the entropy is over the predecessor distribution it is inherently popularity-adjusted.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: Count directed consecutive-item pairs (S_t -> S_{t+1}) over every training sequence, build sparse C, take n_i = sum_j C[j,i], p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i, H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji over observed predecessors, set s_i = exp(H_i), shrink towards sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10} with weight 1/(n_i+1), assign s_i = sbar to items absent from training transitions, then rank-normalise s_i over the 24556 training items and map to r_i. Computed once, offline, before Stage 2, and stored as a frozen buffer.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The statistic reads only training-split sequences; C, sbar, the ranks and r_i are frozen before any Stage 2 or Stage 3 optimisation, no validation or test interaction is touched, validation/test items never contribute counts, and items without training transitions receive the frozen prior sbar rather than any inferred value, so no test-time signal can reach the SID construction.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: c_i = c_max for every item (curvature on, branching signal disconnected), so the Möbius residual chain runs at one constant curvature and the SID is behaviour-blind.
ideas.ablation_both_on: c_i = c_max·(1−H_i) + c_floor, so each item's residual chain and assignment use its own measured branching curvature.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c_i = 0 for every item, so exp_0 and log_0 are the identity and Möbius addition is vector addition; the quantizer is exactly the baseline Euclidean RQ-VAE while H_i is still computed and logged.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 TRAINING sequences only. For every consecutive pair (u_t=i, u_{t+1}=j) inside a training session, increment n_ij. Then p_i(j)=n_ij/Σ_j' n_ij', n_i = number of distinct j with n_ij>0, and H_i = −Σ_j p_i(j) ln p_i(j) / ln(n_i) for n_i≥2; items with n_i<2 or no outgoing training pair get H_i = H̄, the mean of H over items with n_i≥2. The table is built once, frozen before Stage-2 epoch 1, and stored as a 24556-entry vector.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed next-item transition branching of each item — the normalised entropy of its empirical successor distribution (a user-interest branching signal).
ideas.cost_estimate: One offline pre-pass over the training transition table (O(number of training transitions)) and, per step, B·L·K exp-map evaluations for code points plus B·L log/Möbius evaluations for the item residual. At B=256, L=4, K=256, d=64 this is ~2.6e5 vector exp maps and ~0.2 GFLOP per step, under 2% of a baseline step; temporaries are O(B·K·L·d) floats (~67 MB at those sizes) and are chunked over K if memory is tight. Over 3000 epochs × 24 steps = 72k steps the added wall clock stays under about 5%.
ideas.coupling_equation: c_i = c_max·(1 − H_i) + c_floor;  k_l = argmin_k d_P^{c_i}( exp_0^{c_i}(r_l/M_l), exp_0^{c_i}(e_{l,k}/M_l) );  r_{l+1} = log_0^{c_i}( exp_0^{c_i}(r_l/M_l) ⊕_{c_i} (−exp_0^{c_i}(e_{l,k_l}/M_l)) ).
ideas.coupling_path: The item's branching entropy sets c_i; c_i sets the ball; the ball defines both the code points p_{l,k}=exp_0^{c_i}(e_{l,k}/M_l) and the item point q_l=exp_0^{c_i}(r_l/M_l); the Poincaré distance at c_i picks k_l; k_l enters the Möbius residual r_{l+1}=log_0^{c_i}(q_l ⊕_{c_i} (−p_{l,k_l})) feeding level l+1. Behaviour-off freezes c_i at c_max for all items (still curved, no longer item-adaptive); geometry-off sends c_i→0, where exp/log are the identity and Möbius addition is vector addition, i.e. exactly the Euclidean RQ-VAE. Either switch changes the chosen codes and hence the SID tuple.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If successor branching tracks how hierarchical an item's neighbourhood really is, then flattening the metric for broad-branch items (small c_i) and sharpening it for peaked ones (large c_i) makes RQ prefixes split along actual successor clusters, so the Stage-3 model sees more predictable prefixes and test Recall@10 rises above 0.065. Observable as SID reassignment concentrated on items far from the median H_i, a fall in the training prefix conditional entropy of the next item given the current item, and a Recall gain over both switch-off settings even though only the both-on arm is trained.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, on the assignment step and on the residual chain between levels, during Stage-2 training and at SID construction for every item; the decoder and the Stage-3 model stay Euclidean and unchanged.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincaré ball of fixed-form, item-specific negative curvature −c_i, c_i ∈ [c_floor, c_max], with closed-form origin exponential/logarithmic maps, Möbius addition/subtraction, and Poincaré distance d_P^{c_i}.
ideas.key_change: Replace the Euclidean residual r_next = r_l - e_{l,k} with a curved residual r_next = log_0^{c_i}( q_l ⊕_{c_i} (−p_{l,k}) ) where q_l = exp_0^{c_i}(r_l/M_l); the curvature c_i is set by the item's measured successor-branching entropy, and the code is chosen by the Poincaré distance at the same c_i.
ideas.leakage_boundary: H_i uses only within-session transitions of the Stage-2 training split. No validation or test interaction, no Stage-3 input, and no cross-split co-occurrence enters H_i or c_i. The curvature table and c_max are frozen before any validation/test scoring; items that appear only in validation/test receive H̄ and never contribute successor counts.
ideas.motivation: The RQ-VAE residual chain treats every item with the same Euclidean geometry, so a broad, many-way-branching item and a sharply predictable item get their prefixes shaped by the same metric. But an item's successor branching is exactly what decides whether a deep hierarchical prefix helps (peaked successors, tree-like neighbourhood) or hurts (flat, broad branching). A global geometry, or the earlier per-level prefix-hit curvature, cannot express that — and that earlier curvature saturated because a protective cap replaced the signal over the whole operating range.
ideas.novelty: The curvature is PER ITEM, derived from the normalised entropy of that item's training-only successor distribution, and it acts as a Möbius (gyrovector) residual subtraction inside the residual-quantization chain — not as a distance weight, an OT cost, a codebook update, or a codebook-move rule. No cap is needed: the exponential map of any positive curvature lands strictly inside its own ball, so the measured branching spans the whole curvature range with no protective clip. This is not per-level prefix-hit control, not successor-diffused Sinkhorn, not Fréchet codebook updates, not a Lorentz/boost shift.
ideas.observables: (1) fraction of the 24556 items whose level-1 and full SID tuple change versus behaviour-off and versus Euclidean, expected to concentrate on items with extreme H_i; (2) realised deciles of H_i and c_i showing the curvature actually applied, with no clip; (3) training-set conditional entropy of the next item's SID prefix given the current item, which should fall when coupling is on; (4) Stage-3 test_recall@10 against 0.065.

rejected_ideas.reason: out of scope: ablation_geometry_off does not say what replaces the curve

risks: Per-item curvature places the shared codebook at different ball positions for different items, which can blur code semantics or trigger code collapse; H_i is noisy for rare items and for items with fewer than two distinct successors; the curved residual may hurt reconstruction if the tangent-space remainder is not contractive; the gain may be smaller than seed noise, since only one run is made.
ideas.safeguards: artanh argument clamped to 1−1e-7; Möbius denominator clamped to ≥1e-8; c<1e-6 uses the Euclidean branch; if q_rem=0 return r_{l+1}=0; M_l floored at 1e-8 and the per-item denominator max(M_l,‖r‖) guarantees ‖v‖≤1 so the exp map is always defined; items with n_i<2 use H̄ and are never dropped; if c_max is non-finite or ≤0 it is reset to 1.0 and the event is logged; the curvature table is read-only; NaN/Inf guards abort the step rather than silently clipping curvature.
ideas.spec_equations:
Closed forms in the unit ball with curvature −c (c>0):
  exp_0^c(v) = ( tanh(√c·‖v‖/2) / (√c·‖v‖) ) · v
  log_0^c(x) = (2/√c) · artanh(√c·‖x‖) · x/‖x‖
  a ⊕_c b = (1/√c) · [ ((1 + 2⟨ã,b̃⟩ + ‖b̃‖²) ã + (1−‖ã‖²) b̃) / (1 + 2⟨ã,b̃⟩ + ‖ã‖²‖b̃‖²) ], with ã=√c·a, b̃=√c·b
  a ⊖_c b = a ⊕_c (−b)
  d_P^c(x,y) = (2/√c) · artanh( √c · ‖(−x) ⊕_c y‖ )
  All five have the Euclidean limit (v, x, a+b, a−b, ‖x−y‖) as c→0, implemented with a c<1e-6 branch.
Pseudocode per batch:
  for each item i in batch:
    H_i from frozen table; c_i = c_max·(1−H_i)+c_floor
    r = encoder(i)
    for l in 1..L:
      M_l = max(M_l, max_batch‖r‖) with EMA decay 0.99 (M_l initialised to 1.0)
      v = r / max(M_l, ‖r‖, 1e-8)                     # ‖v‖ ≤ 1 always
      q = exp_0^{c_i}(v)
      P = exp_0^{c_i}( e_{l,:} / max(M_l,1e-8) )        # shape K×d
      k_l = argmin_k d_P^{c_i}(q, P[k])
      q_rem = q ⊖_{c_i} P[k_l]
      r = log_0^{c_i}(q_rem)
    z_rec = Σ_l e_{l,k_l}
    loss = ‖z − z_rec‖² + β·commitment (unchanged, β as in baseline)
  SID(i) = (k_1,…,k_L)
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are each training item's encoder vector z, the L codebooks C_l={e_{l,k}}⊂R^d, the frozen per-item entropies H_i, the measured c_max, and the running level scales M_l. Output is the discrete tuple (k_1,…,k_L) and the reconstruction sum of chosen embeddings; the curved intermediates q_l, P, q_rem, r_l are differentiable and used only to choose the code and form the next residual.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. Signal: H_i = normalised Shannon entropy of item i's empirical next-item distribution from consecutive training pairs; curvature c_i = c_max·(1−H_i) + c_floor with c_max = 1/median(‖ẑ^(1)‖²) measured from training encoder outputs during epoch 1, c_floor = 1e-3. Range: H_i ∈ [0,1] by construction, hence c_i ∈ [1e-3, c_max] exactly, with no clip anywhere; the realised deciles of H_i and c_i are logged.

ideas.title: Per-item successor-branching curvature applied as a Möbius residual chain in the RQ-VAE quantizer

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: rho_i = 0.45 for every item (median of the rank map, one radius r = artanh(0.45) = 0.4847, tangent target t_i = 0.4847*zhat_i); curvature and the Poincare score unchanged, so only the behaviour-driven radial separation is removed.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: r_i from the behaviour rank map, exp_0 into the ball, Poincare score at every level, Euclidean reconstruction on t_i.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Same behaviour radii r_i and same tangent target t_i, but score is Euclidean |a-e_lk|^2 and exp_0 is the identity, so codewords are plain bounded Euclidean points and the radial-matching pressure of the curvature disappears.
ideas.behavior_computation: Count directed consecutive-item pairs (S_t -> S_{t+1}) over every training sequence, build sparse C, take n_i = sum_j C[j,i], p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i, H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji over observed predecessors, set s_i = exp(H_i), shrink towards sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10} with weight 1/(n_i+1), assign s_i = sbar to items absent from training transitions, then rank-normalise s_i over the 24556 training items and map to r_i. Computed once, offline, before Stage 2, and stored as a frozen buffer.
ideas.behavior_signal: Behaviour-conditioned context generality: the effective number of distinct predecessor contexts of an item, exp(H_i), from directed item-to-item transitions in the training split; because the entropy is over the predecessor distribution it is inherently popularity-adjusted.
ideas.cost_estimate: One extra pre-training pass over the training transition stream (O(E), sparse COO counts of a few million entries, tens of seconds on CPU, done once, cached as a length-N float vector); no extra parameters, no extra epochs, no extra forward pass. Per step at the frozen scale (batch 1024 = 24556/24, L = 3, K = 256, d = 64): 786432 distance evaluations, about 1.6e8 flops, i.e. roughly one extra elementwise pass over the similarity tensor the baseline already forms, under 1 percent of a step and under 2 percent of an epoch wall-clock.
ideas.coupling_equation: k_l(i) = argmin_k s_P( exp_0( clamp(t_i - sum_{j<l} m_{j k_j(i)}, 0.9) ), exp_0( squash(m_lk) ) ) with t_i = artanh(0.9 * rank(s_i)/(N+1)) * z_i/|z_i|, where s_i is the behaviour context-entropy statistic and s_P is the fixed-curvature (c = 1) Poincare squared-distance kernel.
ideas.coupling_path: The behaviour rank sets the tangent norm r_i, that norm is the argument of exp_0, its image p_i enters the Poincare score against exp_0(m_lk), and the argmin over that score fixes the SID token; the reconstruction target and the residual cascade then run on the same t_i = r_i*zhat. Remove behaviour (r_i constant) and every item sits at one radius so the curved score can only separate angles; remove geometry (Euclidean score) and the radius still exists but the 1/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)) factor is gone, so radial banding no longer dominates and the codeword choice changes.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Worth keeping only if the level-1 prefix is genuinely radius-locked to the behaviour statistic: level-1 prefix ids nearly monotone in rho_i and the mean r_i of the items sharing a level-1 prefix separating strongly across prefixes, with the level-1 prefix becoming more predictable from the same history because it now carries a generality prior. Observable as high Spearman correlation between level-1 prefix index and mean r_i of its members, a drop in level-1 prefix conditional entropy given the previous item on training transitions (diagnostic only), and, as the judgement, Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 from the single frozen run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the quantizer, at every RQ level, inside the nearest-codeword assignment: the codeword is chosen by the curved score between the exponential image of the current tangent residual and the exponential image of the codeword, and the item point itself is produced by exp_0 of the behaviour-radius tangent vector.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (derived from the unit-norm direction normalisation), Poincare exponential map exp_0(v) = tanh(|v|) v/|v|, and the Poincare distance in monotonically transformed squared form s(x,y) = |x-y|^2/((1-|x|^2)(1-|y|^2)), whose arcosh is the geodesic distance.
ideas.key_change: Replace the encoder magnitude by a behaviour-derived rank radius, r_i = artanh(0.9 * rank(s_i)/(N+1)), send the item to the Poincare point p_i = exp_0(r_i * z_i/|z_i|), and choose each RQ level's codeword by argmin of the Poincare distance between exp_0(residual) and exp_0(squashed codeword) instead of the Euclidean distance, while reconstruction and commitment losses stay Euclidean on the same tangent target t_i = r_i * z_i/|z_i|.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The statistic reads only training-split sequences; C, sbar, the ranks and r_i are frozen before any Stage 2 or Stage 3 optimisation, no validation or test interaction is touched, validation/test items never contribute counts, and items without training transitions receive the frozen prior sbar rather than any inferred value, so no test-time signal can reach the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: An RQ-VAE SID prefix is currently a purely semantic token. Nothing in the quantizer forces the coarse prefix to correlate with how generic or context-specific an item is, so the Stage3 generator must learn prefix popularity structure implicitly from short histories. If the first SID level is stratified by a measured, training-only generality statistic, the coarse prefix becomes a cheaply predictable "how generic is this item" token and later levels only refine the angle (fine semantics), which should raise prefix predictability and Stage3 Recall@10.
ideas.novelty: Earlier mechanisms here put behaviour into the quantizer cost (successor mass in a Poincare Sinkhorn cost), into the codebook update (successor-weighted Poincare Frechet means), into the curvature itself (per-level curvature from a hard prefix hit rate), or into a cone/boost/Lorentz-profile/fibre variant, i.e. behaviour always modifies a weight, a curvature, a mean or a translation. Here behaviour modifies the RADIAL COORDINATE of the item point only (a rank map of a measured entropy statistic), curvature is fixed at c = 1 and therefore cannot be saturated by any protective bound, and the geometry acts in the nearest-codeword score through the factor 1/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)), which is exactly what makes radial matching dominate for far items and angular matching dominate for near items. No Sinkhorn, no Frechet update, no cone, no translation, no per-level curvature, no auxiliary loss.
ideas.observables: Level-1 prefix ids nearly monotone in rho_i (high Spearman between prefix index and mean r_i of members); within-prefix spread of r_i shrinks versus the behaviour-off arm; level-1 conditional entropy of the prefix given the previous item drops; level-1 codebook usage concentrates in radially separated bands; reconstruction loss on the same target t compared with the geometry-off arm; and finally Stage3 test_recall@10 from one frozen run, above 0.065.
risks: Discarding encoder magnitude may cost reconstruction, since magnitude carried some frequency information that the cascade must now rebuild from radius; the hyperbolic score may let level-1 codewords collapse onto radial bands and waste angular capacity so levels 2 and 3 do all semantic work; the rank map spreads radii uniformly and may over-weight the tail; the residual clamp at 0.9 may bind at levels 2 and 3 for badly reconstructed items; and Stage3 may already model popularity from the history, in which case a popularity-stratified prefix adds nothing and recall stays flat.
ideas.safeguards: Normalise direction with max(|z|,1e-8); keep rho_i in (0,0.9) so 1-rho_i^2 >= 0.19 and the Poincare denominator never vanishes (the 0.9 margin is applied to the INPUT rank map before artanh, the normalise-first rule, so no protective cap truncates the behaviour statistic: the full rank range 0..1 maps monotonically into 0..0.9 and radius 0..1.4722); clamp tangent norms with min(1, 0.9/|v|) and max(|v|,1e-8) instead of dividing by a possibly zero norm; evaluate the score via s = |a-e|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)) and never via arcosh, avoiding domain errors; add 1e-12 to the denominator; keep the radius buffer requires_grad = False so no gradient drifts it into the boundary; leave items without training transitions at the frozen prior sbar.
ideas.spec_equations: Offline: C[j,i] += 1 per consecutive training pair; n_i = sum_j C[j,i]; p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i; H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji; s_i = (n_i exp(H_i) + sbar)/(n_i+1); sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10}; s_i = sbar if n_i = 0; u_i = rank(s_i)/(N+1); rho_i = 0.9 u_i; r_i = 0.5 log((1+rho_i)/(1-rho_i)). Online per step: zhat = z/max(|z|,1e-8); t = r_i*zhat; u = t; for l in 1..L: a = u*min(1, 0.9/max(|u|,1e-8)); m = m_l*min(1, 0.9/|m_l|); e = tanh(|m|)*m/|m|; s_lk = |a-e_lk|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e_lk|^2)); k_l = argmin_k s_lk; u = u - m_l[k_l]; t_hat = sum_l m_l[k_l]; L_total = |t-t_hat|^2 + beta|t-sg(t_hat)|^2 + |sg(t)-t_hat|^2; SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder output z in R^d for the batch (d = 64), frozen per-item radius buffer r in R^N, L tangent codebooks m_l in R^{K x d} (L = 3, K = 256), flags behaviour_on and geometry_on. Outputs: per-item SID tuple (k_1,...,k_L), tangent reconstruction t_hat, scalar loss; the only state reaching Stage 3 is the emitted SIDs (radii frozen, codebooks read only through the SIDs).

specification.text: (1) Precompute from training sequences only: C[j,i] = directed counts of consecutive items, n_i = sum_j C[j,i], p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i, H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji, s_i = (n_i*exp(H_i) + sbar)/(n_i+1) with sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10}, and s_i = sbar for items never observed. (2) rank_i = rank of s_i over the N = 24556 training items (ties by id), u_i = rank_i/(N+1) in (0,1), rho_i = 0.9*u_i, r_i = artanh(rho_i) in (0, 1.4722). (3) Per step: zhat = z/max(|z|,1e-8), t = r_i*zhat, u = t; for l = 1..L: a = u*min(1, 0.9/max(|u|,1e-8)), e_lk = tanh(|m_lk|)*m_lk/|m_lk| with m_lk the level-l tangent codebook after squash min(1,0.9/|m_lk|), score s_lk = |a-e_lk|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e_lk|^2)), k_l = argmin_k s_lk, u = u - m_lk; t_hat = sum_l m_lk_l; loss = |t-t_hat|^2 + beta|t - sg(t_hat)|^2 + |sg(t) - t_hat|^2 with the baseline beta; emit SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L). (4) Curvature c = 1 is derived, not tuned: after direction normalisation |zhat| = 1, so the unit tangent scale is the encoder scale and the ball radius is 1/sqrt(c) = 1. Remaining constants are documented defaults: 0.9 boundary margin, 1 Laplace prior count, baseline beta.

ideas.title: Behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment: training-transition context entropy sets each item's hyperbolic radius, curvature sets the quantizer score

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: p(j|i) := 0, so v_b = 0 and g = sg[x - e_{l,k}]; the curved chart, geodesic assignment and geodesic commitment remain, isolating the behavioural tangent.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the single trained run, with p(j|i) from the training split and c_l = 1/(4 s_l^2), the transported gated tangent active.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c_l := 0 with an explicit Euclidean code path, so exp_0 = log_x = PT = identity, d_c = Euclidean distance, and the same p-weighted successor difference e_{l,k'(j)} - e_{l,k} enters the gradient; the behaviour term remains, isolating the curvature.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the training split only, counting consecutive (i_t, i_{t+1}) pairs, keeping the top-M=16 successors per item and dividing by the row count; the table is frozen at epoch 0 and rebuilt only from training data. No popularity correction is applied (documented default), so nothing is tuned.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions from training sequences, aggregated into a sparse row-stochastic successor distribution p(j|i) per item, top-M truncated and renormalized.
ideas.cost_estimate: Transition table is built once from the training split (24556 x 16 ints, ~0.4M entries). Per step at the frozen scale (batch ~1023, L=4 levels, M=16 successors) there are about 65k log-map + transport evaluations of dimension d (d=32-64), roughly 4-8 MFLOP, plus one Mobius add per item per level; expected overhead 3-8% of step time over 72,000 steps (24 x 3000), no extra forward passes and no extra epochs. The s_l and delta_l measurements are one pass over 24556 latents.
ideas.coupling_equation: g_i,l = sg[x - e_{l,k}] + [ d_{c_l}(x,e_{l,k}) / (d_{c_l}(x,e_{l,k}) + delta_l) ] * PT_{e_{l,k}->x}^{c_l}( sum_{j in Succ(i)} p(j|i) * log_{e_{l,k}}^{c_l}( e_{l,k'(j)} ) ), with x = exp_0^{c_l}(z_{i,l}/s_l) and c_l = 1/(4 s_l^2).
ideas.coupling_path: p(j|i) selects and weights successor codewords; the log map at the assigned codeword and the parallel transport to the latent are defined only by the curvature c_l; their output is the gradient the encoder receives. Setting p=0 zeroes the term, and setting c=0 replaces log/transport by Euclidean differences, so both factors are load-bearing in one path.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If SID quality is limited by the encoder not knowing which items are behaviourally reachable from which, then transporting successor tangents into the quantizer gradient should pull high-branch items toward their successor region, raising training prefix top-1 transition accuracy and Stage3 test Recall@10 above the no-transport baseline. Observed as a nonzero SID assignment flip rate (target >2% of items versus epoch 0), a monotone rise in prefix transition predictability, and a Recall@10 improvement with both switches on.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: At quantization time (latent injection, assignment, commitment) and in the backward pass, where the transported tangent is added to the straight-through gradient. It is not a side loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of trainable-free curvature -c_l with c_l = 1/(4 s_l^2) (so the ball radius is 2 s_l, twice the measured latent scale), exponential map exp_0, logarithmic map log_x, geodesic distance d_c, and parallel transport PT_{x->y}; all in closed form.
ideas.key_change: Each level carries a curvature c_l derived from the measured latent scale; the latent is injected into that ball through exp_0, quantized by geodesic distance, and the STE gradient is augmented by the tangent vector of its training successors, parallel-transported from the codeword to the latent and gated by the current commit distance.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Counts, s_l, delta_l and the successor-to-codeword map are computed exclusively from the training split and from the current training codebook; validation and test sequences are never read, and no evaluation statistic enters any constant.
ideas.motivation: In a VQ/RQ-VAE the straight-through estimator hands the encoder a pure reconstruction gradient, so the training transition structure (which item a user actually takes next) never reaches the encoder or the codebook geometry: SID assignment is blind to behavioural reachability. Curved space has so far been used only to re-weight losses, assignments or codebook means, never to shape the gradient that actually moves the latent.
ideas.novelty: Unlike the per-level curvature controllers, Poincare Sinkhorn/mass transport, curved Frechet codebook updates and prefix-cone proposals, this changes neither the assignment rule nor a loss value: it changes the vector that backpropagates through the quantizer. The successor distribution is log-mapped at the assigned codeword and parallel-transported to the latent, in the same Poincare ball that defines the quantizer commit and the decoder chart.
ideas.observables: SID assignment flip rate relative to epoch 0; per-level prefix top-1 transition accuracy on training transitions; codebook usage entropy per level; geodesic commit distance distribution; Stage3 test Recall@10.
risks: Transport is noisy under sparse transitions; the successor codeword map k'(j) is stale within an epoch; curvature from s_l drifts as the encoder rescales; the added tangent could dominate reconstruction and collapse codebook usage; the effect may be below seed noise in a single run.
ideas.safeguards: Use c_l = 1/(4 s_l^2) so |x| < 2 s_l for every |z| <= s_l, which keeps x strictly inside the ball by construction, with no protective cap on the curvature; clamp the Mobius argument |(-x)+_c y| <= (1-1e-6)/sqrt(c); artanh uses the log form for small arguments and clamps at 1-1e-6; norms divided by max(|.|, 1e-12); lambda_l floored at 1e-6 and the soft bound r_l tanh(|.|/r_l) is injective over the observed range, so it never freezes the behaviour term; the successor map is stop-grad and recomputed once per epoch; delta_l > 0 by construction from a median over 24556 items.
ideas.spec_equations: exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)|v|) * v/(sqrt(c)|v|); log_x^c(y) = (2/(sqrt(c) lambda_x)) * artanh(sqrt(c)|(-x)+_c y|) * ((-x)+_c y)/|(-x)+_c y|; d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)|(-x)+_c y|); lambda_x = 2/(1-c|x|^2); PT_{x->y}^c(v) = (lambda_x/lambda_y) * gyr[y,-x] v; c_l = 1/(4 s_l^2); z_hat = z/s_l; x = exp_0^{c_l}(z_hat); k = argmin_k d_{c_l}(x,e_{l,k}); v_b = sum_j p(j|i) log_{e_{l,k}}^{c_l}(e_{l,k'(j)}); v_soft = r_l tanh(|lambda_l v_b|/r_l) * lambda_l v_b/|lambda_l v_b|, r_l = 0.5/sqrt(c_l); kappa = u/(u+delta_l), u = d_{c_l}(x,e_{l,k}); g = sg[x-e_{l,k}] + kappa * PT_{e_{l,k}->x}^{c_l}(v_soft); L_commit = u^2.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: per-level latent z_{i,l}, current codebook {e_{l,k}}, training successor table p(j|i), measured s_l, delta_l, lambda_l, and the switch flags. Output: the encoder-side gradient g_{i,l}, the assigned codeword index k, the scalar geodesic commitment loss, and the updated codebook (through the same distance).

specification.text: For level l, measure s_l = max over the 24556 training latents of |z_l| (one pass at epoch 0, refreshed every 100 epochs), set c_l = 1/(4 s_l^2). Map x = exp_0^{c_l}(z/s_l). Assign k = argmin_k d_{c_l}(x, e_{l,k}). Build the training-only successor distribution p(j|i) (top-M=16, renormalized). v_b = sum_j p(j|i) log_{e_{l,k}}^{c_l}(e_{l,k'(j)}), where k'(j) is j's current level-l codeword (stop-grad). Scale lambda_l = delta_l / mean|v_b| measured at epoch 0, delta_l = median commit distance at epoch 0; apply the curvature-tied soft bound r_l tanh(|lambda_l v_b|/r_l) with r_l = 0.5/sqrt(c_l). Gradient to encoder: g = sg[x - e_{l,k}] + kappa * PT_{e_{l,k}->x}^{c_l}(v_b_soft), kappa = d_c(x,e_{l,k})/(d_c(x,e_{l,k})+delta_l). Commitment loss is the squared geodesic distance d_{c_l}(x,e_{l,k})^2, so the codebook update is also curved. Autograd differentiates exp_0. Three switches: USE_BEHAV (v_b=0 when off) and USE_HYPER (c_l=0, Euclidean branch when off); the single run has both on.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
